clauses.title: Scope – Requirement for
clauses.text: 1. Scope - Requirement for non-ferrous metal sliding door bolts (aldrops)  commonly used in general building construction for locking doors, gates etc. with padlocks.

clauses.title: Types
clauses.text: 2. Types Type 1— Brass sliding door bolts with sand cast brass hasp, staple and fixing bolts or clips and rolled or drawn brass bolts. Type 2— Brass sliding door bolts with  die-cast brass hasp, staple and fixing  bolts or clips and rolled or drawn brass bolts. Type 3 — Aluminium alloy sliding door bolts with hasp, staple and fixing clips of sheets, or extruded sections and fixing bolts and  sliding bolts of extruded sections of  aluminium alloy.

clauses.title: Materials – Shall comply
clauses.text: 3. Materials - Shall comply with the requirements given in Table 1 of the standard.

clauses.title: Dimensions
clauses.text: 4. Dimensions Type Size, mm 1 and 2 150, 200, 250, 300, 375 and 450 3 200, 250, 300, 350, 375 and 450 Note— For details of dimensions and tolerance see Tables 2 and 3 read with Fig. 1 of the standard.

clauses.title: Finish
clauses.text: 5. Finish —  Brass sliding door bolts  shall  have satin finish or shall be polished or plated. Aluminium shall be anodiezed to a bright, natural, sat or satin finish or dyed. For detailed information, refer to IS  2681 : 1993 Specification for non-ferrous metal  sliding door  bolts (aldrops) for use with padlocks (third  revision). SUMMARY OF IS 2681 : 1993 NON-FERROUS METAL SLIDING DOOR BOLTS (ALDROPS) FOR USE WITH PADLOCKS (Third Revision) 1. Scope - Requirements for  exposed type hydraulically regulated door closers for vertical hinge type doors opening to one side only and weighing more than 80 kg.  This does not cover the requirements for concealed type hydraulic door closers and also the pneumatic or mechanical type of door closers. 4. Materials i) Non porous body   Cast iron /Aluminium and back plate alloy / Zinc alloy ii) Piston or Pack- Cast iron / Steel piston / pinion Aluminium alloy/Zinc alloy Note— For materials for other components see 7 and Table 2 of the standard. 5. Essential  Requirements

clauses.title: The closer shall be
clauses.text: 5.1 The closer shall be manufactured in three sizes conforming to the requirements given in Table 1, in accordance with the direction of  the opening of the door either clockwise or anti-clockwise.

clauses.title: The closing time shall
clauses.text: 5.2 The closing time shall be easily adjustable between 5 and 20 seconds by means of regualting  screw.

clauses.title: Hydraulic oil filling shall
clauses.text: 5.3 Hydraulic oil filling shall work satisfactorily at all temperatures between 50 ºC and -10 ºC without requiring any change except adjustment of the regulating screw.

clauses.title: The closer shall
clauses.text: 5.4 The closer shall  be capable  to regulate the speed by extending spring or  adjustment  in  control  valve screw, as the case may be.

clauses.title: Performance Requirements
clauses.text: 6.1 Performance Requirements — When opened through 90º , the door shall  swing back to an angle of 20    5º with normal speed, but thereafter the speed should get automatically retarded and should smoothly negotiate with the latch (where provided)

clauses.title: Endurance Test
clauses.text: 6.2 Endurance Test — After 50,000 operations against maximum load specified, the closer shall show no defects, failure or leakage of oil  etc. Note — For test details see Annex B of the standard.

clauses.title: Finish
clauses.text: 7. Finish — Polished or painted and finished with lacquer  In case of aluminium body, it may be anodized. Mild steel parts shall be pickled and given phosphate treatment. Note—For methods of test, refer to Annex B of the standard. For  detailed information, refer to IS 3564 : 1995  Specification for hydraulically regulated door closers (fourth revision).
